text:
Janet: hi folks, I'm Janet — excited to join the runtime team today. Trying to build from source in the recommended dev container but hit a weird ptxas/linker combo error. Any quick onboarding tips?

Janet: build excerpt:
```bash
[ 21%] Building CXX object src/CMakeFiles/llm_runtime.dir/main.cpp.o
ptxas info    : 0 bytes gmem, 0 bytes cmem[0]
ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_90' is not valid for option 'gpu-name'
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lnvidia-ml
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Mika: welcome! :tada: two quick diagnostics: 1) check host `nvidia-smi` driver version; 2) run `nvcc --version` inside the container. Looks like either arch flags or driver/toolkit mismatch.

Rosie: also watch out for image tags. If your host driver is older than the container's CUDA toolkit you get missing libs. If the arch is sm_90 and your GPU doesn't support it, nvcc complains.

Janet: `nvidia-smi` on host shows Driver Version: 530.30.0 and GPU is RTX A2000 (sm_86). Inside container nvcc reports CUDA 12.2.

Natanael: there's your mismatch: container targeting sm_90 but A2000 is sm_86. Two fixes: set CUDAARCHS to only include sm_86 or pick a base image with CUDA that defaults to sm_80/86. In our CMake we honor the CUDA_ARCH environment var: `export CUDAARCHS=sm_86` then `make clean && make -j8`.

Rosie: about `-lnvidia-ml`: that lib is part of the NVIDIA driver utilities (NVML). If the container can't find it at link time, ensure you're not overriding LD_LIBRARY_PATH with host paths, and don't bind-mount /usr/lib/nvidia into the container. We usually rely on the container's packaged cuda libs and the runtime driver mounted by nvidia-container-toolkit.

Janet: tried `export CUDAARCHS=sm_86` then rebuild — ptxas error gone, but now linker still complains about `-lnvidia-ml`. I see `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so` on host but not inside container.

Mika: that's expected. The container shouldn't need the host copy at build-time; however some build scripts try to link against NVML for telemetry. Check `grep -R "nvidia-ml" build | sed -n '1,5p'` to find who adds it. If it's optional, guard it behind `IF(NVML_FOUND)` in CMake. For quick unblock, you can install `libnvidia-ml-dev` inside the container image but prefer adjusting the build.

Natanael: also check `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and any pkg-config that resolves NVML. We patched the repo to make NVML optional last quarter; maybe your branch reintroduced it. Run `git status` and check for local CMake tweaks.

Janet: I found a legacy plugin in third_party/telemetry that links NVML unconditionally. Removing that link flag fixed the build locally. Binary runs in container.

build-bot: note: created GH issue #1587 to make NVML link optional during cmake configure.

Rosie: great catch. Please add a short onboarding note about RTX A2000+CUDA12 quirks (sm_86 default) to the runtime setup doc.

Janet: will do. Thanks all — tagging @Mika @Natanael if I need a quick review on the GH change. :thumbsup:
